evals.name: compute-mfu-correctly
evals.prompt: 7B non-embedding params, 8 H100s, global batch 256, seq len 4096, 18.9 s per step. What's our MFU?
evals.expected_output: MFU = 6*N*B*s / (T*P_peak*n) with dense 989 TFLOP/s: about 33%, and flags the sparse-peak trap.

assertions.description: Gives MFU = 6·N·tokens_per_step / (T · P_peak · n) or equivalent
Uses the dense H100 bf16 peak of ~989 TFLOP/s and warns against the 1979 sparse figure
Produces a numeric MFU in the roughly 30–35% range
Shows the intermediate token count and FLOP count rather than just asserting a percentage

evals.name: mfu-vs-hfu
evals.prompt: MFU랑 HFU가 뭐가 달라? activation recomputation 켜면 어떻게 돼?
evals.expected_output: MFU counts model-definition FLOPs, HFU counts all executed FLOPs; under full recompute HFU/MFU ~ 8/6 ~ 1.33; MFU <= HFU always; MFU is the cross-system metric.

assertions.description: Defines MFU as model-required FLOPs and HFU as all FLOPs the hardware executed
States that under full recomputation HFU/MFU is about 8/6 ≈ 1.33
States MFU ≤ HFU always
Says MFU is the number to compare across systems because it is invariant to the recomputation choice

evals.name: 6n-breaks-at-long-context
evals.prompt: 6N FLOPs per token 공식이 항상 맞아? 언제 안 맞아?
evals.expected_output: Breaks when attention dominates: attention fraction is s/(6h), so it exceeds 50% of FLOPs when s > 6h. Cites the Megatron correction term.

assertions.description: States 6N counts only parameterized matmuls and omits the attention score computation, which has no parameters
Gives the attention fraction as s/(6h) or equivalently that attention exceeds 50% of FLOPs when s > 6h
Gives a concrete threshold, e.g. that at h=4096 the crossover is around s≈24576
Notes that at long context 6N undercounts, so MFU computed from it is understated

evals.name: scaling-efficiency-diagnosis
evals.prompt: GPU 8장 썼는데 5.2배밖에 안 빨라졌어. 이거 심각한 거야? 뭐부터 확인해야 해?
evals.expected_output: 5.2/8 = 65% strong-scaling efficiency; asks strong vs weak first, then compute-to-comm ratio 6*b*m*s/bytes, then whether the 8 GPUs cross a node boundary, then step-time variance.

assertions.description: Computes the efficiency as about 65% (5.2/8)
Asks or states whether this is strong or weak scaling, and notes they have different expectations
Raises whether the 8 GPUs cross a node boundary, since NVLink to fabric is a large step down
Brings up the compute-to-communication ratio, e.g. 6·b·m·s per wire byte, and that raising m or b improves it
Suggests checking whether step time is stable or variable, to separate bandwidth from straggler/bubble

evals.name: loss-changed-after-config-change
evals.prompt: TP를 1에서 2로 바꿨더니 loss curve가 달라졌어. parallelism은 수학적으로 같아야 하는 거 아니야?
evals.expected_output: Yes it should be identical; the first suspect is that B = b*m*d changed because t does not multiply the batch; then token-weighted loss, per-axis RNG seeding, and data sharding by n instead of d.

assertions.description: Identifies B = b·m·d as the first thing to check, and that t (tensor parallel) does not multiply the batch
Explains that ranks in a TP group process the same samples, so raising t at fixed n halves d and therefore halves B
Raises token-weighted loss versus mean-of-per-rank-means as a possible cause
Raises RNG seeding — dropout must differ across DP ranks but be identical within a TP group
Affirms that parallelism should not change the mathematics, so this is a correctness bug not a tuning issue

evals.name: realistic-mfu-expectations
evals.prompt: What MFU do the best large training runs actually achieve? Our run is at 41% — is that bad?
evals.expected_output: Cites PaLM 46.2%, Megatron 52% of peak, MegaScale 55.2%, Llama 3 38-43%; 41% is normal; flags that >60% warrants an audit of the three inflations.

assertions.description: Cites at least two specific published MFU figures with their runs (e.g. PaLM 46.2%, MegaScale 55.2%, Llama 3 38–43%)
Concludes 41% is a normal, healthy number rather than a problem
Conveys that the best engineered runs land roughly in the high 30s to mid 50s
Notes that a much higher claim warrants auditing how FLOPs were counted — sparse peak, counting recompute, or including embeddings
